name: ASL Airlines group scheme
description: White aircraft. 'ASL AIRLINES' on the forward fuselage in italic capitals, ASL heavy and navy, AIRLINES lighter and light blue, over a light-blue blade swooping down and back from under the A. The fin's top is navy, cut off below by a line that falls slightly toward the trailing edge; under a white wedge that closes toward the trailing edge, the fin's lower part is light blue, its top edge curving up from the leading edge's root. The winglets the same, navy above light blue. White engines.

areas.name: light-blue blade under the title, from under the A down and back to a point
light-blue lower fin, its top edge curving up from the leading edge's root to meet the navy at the trailing edge
light blue on the winglet's lower part

titles.style: 'AIRLINES' straight after, in lighter, widely spaced italic capitals, light blue.
On the right, 'AIRLINES' forward, after 'ASL' read from the tail.

logos.description: Small Austrian and European flags side by side above the registration, behind the aft door (the 747s are on the Austrian register).

notes: Measured on OE-IFB (747-400ERF, left side from below, Leipzig, 2025-03-02) fitted to the 747-400F shape; OE-IFM (2026, right), OE-IFD (2024, left) and OE-ILC (2022, the maintainer's sighting) wear the same. The fin carries no logo: the navy top and light-blue lower band are the mark, drawn as areas; the navy's lower edge runs from y 0.41 at the leading edge to 0.32 at the trailing edge, the light blue's top edge from the leading edge's root up to meet it there. The titles' baseline reads 0.12 at ASL to 0.34 at the end of AIRLINES in this fit (the camera is 13° below and the title is level in the photo: perspective), drawn level at 0.2 with cap height 0.2 (the fit reads 0.17 at ASL to 0.26 at the end of AIRLINES); ASL x 0.161-0.208, AIRLINES 0.217-0.323. The blade under the title is placed relative to the title (low): from under the A down and back to a point at about x 0.25, about 0.6 m deep at its root. The right side's order (ASL aft) is from OE-IFD (2024). ASL Airlines Belgium's 737s and the group's other airlines (ASL Airlines France, FPO; ASL Airlines Ireland, ABR, whose tagged jets wear Amazon's Prime Air paint) use the same scheme as far as photos show; not drawn or tagged here.
history: New 2026-11-22 (the maintainer's sightings: OE-ILC). The scheme replaced TNT Airways' orange after ASL bought it in 2016.
